Again not true. The amount of money Spotify and other streaming companies pay out to rights holders is at an all time high. That is because payouts are based on an agreed percentage of revenue. More revenue = higher royalty payout.  What is going down is the per stream average value, which is an irrelevant number in this formula. 

I'm not saying Spotify is without criticism, but it's shared by Apple too, and maybe most of all, the major labels. 

The problem is too many people here don't want to understand the business of music streaming and music royalties and just boil it down to "Spotify doesn't pay artists enough."

text:
Well, yeah, they’re competing with YouTube, Amazon, Audible, Apple Music, Tidal, etc. Spotify has the largest share of users across all streaming services so it makes sense that they’d want to capitalize on where their users are.

TBH it comes down to how you use Spotify. If you open the app and expect the Home Screen to feed you recommendations, then yeah, it’s going to feel cluttered and you’ll see things you don’t want. If you use the library to browse what you’ve saved and playlists you’ve built, or the search tab to find new music, you have more control over what you see.
